name: Garrison Institute
technique: Mindfulness, meditation, and contemplative practice drawn from many traditions (varies by visiting teacher)
influences: New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care
teacherAccess: Visiting teachers change with each program (e.g., Sharon Salzberg, Tsoknyi Rinpoche, Rupert Spira, Zen and Insight teachers, DharmaPunx NYC); most retreats include daily talks, guided sits, and some small-group or dialogue access with the teacher(s).
retreatOptions: Day and evening programs plus residential retreats ranging from 2-3 night weekends to 6-7 night intensives, some with a livestream/online option.
about: The Garrison Institute is a nonsectarian, nonprofit contemplative retreat and research center housed in a renovated 1923 Capuchin Franciscan monastery on the 95-acre former Glenclyffe estate overlooking the Hudson River in Garrison, New York. Founded in 2003 by Diana Calthorpe Rose and Jonathan F. P. Rose as a 'monastery for the 21st century,' it hosts residential meditation and mindfulness retreats led by a rotating roster of outside teachers spanning Buddhist, secular-mindfulness, nondual, yogic, and other contemplative lineages, alongside its own programs on resilience, planetary health, and spirituality and social change. It is not affiliated with a single tradition; each retreat's content, format, and cost are set by the visiting teacher or organization renting the space. The site sleeps up to 165 overnight guests in single, double, and dorm-style rooms with shared bathrooms and no elevator, and serves vegetarian meals in a communal dining hall.
schedule: Programs run on a published calendar of externally-led and Institute-run retreats year-round, most commonly Thursday/Friday–Sunday weekends or 6-7 night intensives; there is no standing daily open-sit schedule outside of scheduled retreats.
cost: Each retreat sets its own all-inclusive program, lodging, and meals fee (varies by teacher/organizer), typically tiered by room type (single, double/twin, dorm/shared, or commuter without lodging); need-based scholarships and a Many Voices Fund for BIPOC applicants are available for some programs.

pricePerDay.notes: Derived from a 6-night residential retreat (Tsoknyi Rinpoche, Sept 2025): dorm $1,330, double $1,420, single $1,570 total per person, including ~$400 program tuition, lodging, and 3 vegetarian meals/day. Prices vary significantly by visiting teacher and program; comparable 7-night retreats have run $2,840-$3,275 total per person.

foodNotes: Three vegetarian (often lacto-vegetarian) meals per day included with residential registration; gluten/dairy-free options generally available on request depending on the retreat.
workNotes: No work/service practice is required of retreatants; the Institute is staffed and catered.
